title: Obesity Surgery risque de mortalité score (OS-MRS)
formula:
The OS-MRS is calculated by the addition of the selected points:

| Variable | Points | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| BMI ≥50 kg/m 2 | No | 0 |
| Yes | 1 | |
| Male gender | No | 0 |
| Yes | 1 | |
| Hypertension | No | 0 |
| Yes | 1 | |
| Risk of PE i.e., OHS, venous stasis ulcers, previous PE, and/or previous IVC filter | No | 0 |
| Yes | 1 | |
| Age ≥45 years | No | 0 |
| Yes | 1 | |

how_to_use.why:
- May help facilitate the informed consent process for bariatric surgery and guide surgical decision-making.
- Provides some standardization for outcome comparisons between surgical treatment centers, which may have variations in their case risk levels.
how_to_use.when: Can be used to predict mortality risk during the preoperative assessment for patients undergoing gastric bypass surgery.
how_to_use.pearls:
- This tool was originally derived from data regarding patients undergoing primary bariatric operations, namely open and laparoscopic Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (RYGB). Subsequent studies have evaluated its use for other bariatric procedures.
- Results should not necessarily rule patients out for surgery, since high-risk patients may greatly benefit from gastric bypass procedures.
- The assessment does not take into account surgeon and institutional experience.
- Factors to consider in assessing postoperative PE risk may include venous stasis, obesity-hypoventilation syndrome, right heart failure, pulmonary hypertension, and previous venous thromboembolism.

next_steps.management: Consider risk reduction strategies for individuals at highest risk of mortality (Class C). These strategies may include choosing lower-risk procedures, opting for staged or sequential treatment approaches, or increasing emphasis on a preoperative reduction in BMI.

more_info:
Interpretation:

| --- | --- | --- |
| A | 0-1 | 0.31% |
| B | 2-3 | 1.90% |
| C | 4-5 | 7.56% |
